|lore=A political agenda is no use without supporters. And in the world of politics, left and right often meet in the middle.
|game_text=Target an opponent's character at Galactic Senate if you have a senator there with a matching agenda. For remainder of turn: your senator's politics is increased by target's current politics, and target's politics is then reduced to zero.
|joke=Left and right "meet in the middle" on the same payroll, as when big donors in the 1996 United States elections gave to both parties.<ref name="nyt-1996">[https://archive.nytimes.com/www.nytimes.com/library/politics/1226campaign-funds.html In Political Money Game, the Year of Big Loopholes], David E. Rosenbaum, ''The New York Times'' (26 December 1996). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260625053046/https://archive.nytimes.com/www.nytimes.com/library/politics/1226campaign-funds.html Internet Archive], 25 June 2026.</ref> A 1907 cartoon, "The Fat Boy in Politics", shows a fat man feeding both the Democratic donkey and the Republican elephant.<ref name="b13-fatboy">[https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:The_Fat_Boy_In_Politics_-_DPLA_-_869b9543e1af8c6af5052e2d72ecf880.jpg The Fat Boy In Politics], Wikimedia Commons, from Hennepin County Library (cartoon by Charles Lewis Bartholomew, ''The Minneapolis Journal'', 5 April 1907). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261027000859/https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:The_Fat_Boy_In_Politics_-_DPLA_-_869b9543e1af8c6af5052e2d72ecf880.jpg Internet Archive], 27 October 2026.</ref> See [[Jokes#On The Payroll Of The Trade Federation|Jokes]].
